title: SLO operational lab: stakeholder scenarios & initiative
content:
One-line summary:
This notebook captures an experiment-first, cross-functional approach to operationalizing SLOs for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated pools) by running a small series of scenario-driven sprints (the "Operational Lab"). It focuses on actionable stakeholder scenarios, acceptance criteria, and a communications/hand-off pattern so feature teams can adopt SLOs without heavy ops debt.

Context / why now:
- We have many SLO designs but inconsistent adoption across product teams; handoffs to SRE and platform are ad hoc.
- Model-serving introduces unique failure modes (KV cache poisoning, long-tail spike from batched requests, quantized-model variance) that require executable runbooks and rehearsed stakeholder flows.
- Leadership asked for a repeatable, low-friction path to go from SLO conception -> 30-day operational readiness.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Publish a repeatable 6-week Operational Lab template that a product team can complete with SRE and Platform support.
   - Success metric: 4 pilot teams complete in Q1 with green canary rollouts.
2) Create 3 scenario-driven runbooks (latency spike, model-accuracy regression, capacity scarcity) mapped to concrete SLOs and playbooks.
   - Success metric: <30m mean time to remediation during tabletop exercises.
3) Reduce friction for SLO onboarding by publishing a one-click checklist (confluence + automated healthboard) and an SDK snippet for SLO signal exports.
   - Success metric: onboarding time drop from ~4 weeks to <=2 weeks.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Focus: model-serving endpoints (generation/chat + embeddings) on Hosted API and Dedicated deployments.
- Exclude: Private on-prem install details (we will capture as a follow-up appendix).
- Timebox: 6-week pilot template + 3 scenario runbooks.

Primary stakeholders & roles:
- Product owner (feature team): owns target SLO definition, user-impact framing, and dataset/eval inputs.
- SRE (this doc owner): crafts runbook, on-call coverage, and escalation path.
- Platform/Serving runtime: provides capacity profiles, autoscale knobs, and fallback model variants.
- Developer Experience: ships SDK snippet and test harness for synthetic traffic.
- Customer Success / Support: defines customer-visible SLAs and playbook steps to surface incidents.

Sprint architecture (Operational Lab template) — 6-week cadence (high level):
Week 0: kickoff + clarity
  - Kickoff workshop (1.5h): align on user journeys, critical SLOs, and business consequences. Invite: product, eng, platform, SRE, CS.
  - Deliverable: SLO charter doc (template) with objective and objective quantification.
Week 1: observable & attack-surface mapping
  - Map telemetry sources (latency histograms, error codes, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, model quality evals).
  - Identify ownership of each signal.
Week 2: runbook drafting + synthetic harness
  - Draft scenario runbooks (latency spike, accuracy regression, capacity scarcity).
  - Platform team provides synthetic traffic harness + load profile.
Week 3: tabletop + instrumentation fixes
  - Tabletop testing for each scenario; collect timing and gaps.
  - Instrument missing metrics and create dashboard widgets.
Week 4: canary strategy & safety net configuration
  - Define canary gates (P95 latency, error rate thresholds, model-quality delta).
  - Configure automatic fallback policies (e.g., fallback to smaller quantized variant or region failover) in routing rules.
Week 5: smoke canary + postmortem template
  - Run real canary with progressive traffic ramp; validate runbooks.
  - Complete postmortem and remediation plan.
Week 6: handoff + cadence establishment
  - Handoff package: runbook, dashboard links, SLO charter, on-call play script, incident comms template.
  - Establish weekly cadence for first 30 days (alerts, health checks).

Example scenario runbook (latency spike from cache miss storm) — condensed:
- Trigger: sustained P95 increase > 200ms above baseline for 5m + KV cache miss rate > 20%
- First 3 minutes (detect & notify): automated alert -> SRE bridge, slack channel #ops-model-serving-alerts, pinned observability dashboard.
- Triage steps:
  1) Check platform autoscale events and GPU utilization (node-level heat map).
  2) Inspect KV cache eviction and prefix cache metrics; run the synthetic prefix query in the harness.
  3) If cache miss storm confirmed, flip route to warm-cache fallback pool (routing policy v2) and trigger cache prefill job.
- Escalation: if recovery > 15 minutes or errors increasing, execute regional fallback and open incident with oncall.
- Post-incident: capture timeline, root cause, and update SLO burn budget ledger.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done for a pilot team:
- SLO charter exists and is approved by Product & SRE.
- Scenario runbooks implemented and tested in tabletop (3 scenarios).
- Dashboards show correct signals (latency hist, error codes, cache stats, model-quality) and are included in the team healthboard.
- Canary gating configured and one successful canary run executed.
- Handoff package created and reviewed with CS and Support.

Signals & dashboards to standardize (minimum viable):
- Latency: P50, P95, P99 for request paths; tail token generation time for streaming.
- Errors: HTTP 5xx breakdown, model-serving rejection rates (quota/validation), and timeouts.
- Capacity: GPU utilization, queue length, in-flight tokens, batch size distribution.
- Quality signals: eval-set perplexity/delta, fallback-model accuracy delta, A/B user metric (if applicable).
- Business surface: requests impacted (daily/monthly), revenue-affecting routes.

Risk register & mitigations (top 5):
1) Risk: Feature teams don't allocate cycles -> Mitigation: reserve 2 SRE days per sprint + executive sponsorship.
2) Risk: Observability gaps for token-level timelines -> Mitigation: lightweight SDK snippet to annotate traces and emit token timing events.
3) Risk: Canary fails silently due to gating misconfig -> Mitigation: run pre-canary dry-run with synthetic user traffic and manual checkpoint.
4) Risk: Cross-team confusion on fallback model tradeoffs -> Mitigation: publish short tech note on quantization quality tradeoffs and default fallback policies.
5) Risk: Customer-facing SLAs conflict -> Mitigation: CS reviews SLO charter in week0; escalate to legal if required.

Communications plan (how we coordinate):
- Weekly sync (30m) for lab pilot teams; standing invites for product, SRE, platform.
- #ops-model-serving-alerts (Slack): incident chatter and quick triage.
- Channels for artifacts: Confluence page for the lab + dedicated GitHub repo for runbook automation.
- Stakeholder update digest: 1-pager after each pilot completion (to execs and GTM).

Operational handoff checklist (deliverable for sign-off):
- Finalized SLO charter (signed by product + SRE).
- Runbooks for top 3 scenarios + link to synthetic harness.
- Dashboards + alert rules (links).
- Canary playbook + traffic ramp schedule.
- Postmortem template and weekly check-in cadence for 30 days.

Metrics to track across pilots (for program-level evaluation):
- Time-to-onboard (days from kickoff to canary).
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) during tabletop & real events.
- Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for each scenario.
- SLO burn rate during the first 30 days post-handoff.
- Number of changes to runbook after first incident.

Open questions / decisions needed (for next leadership sync):
- Do we require feature teams to use the standardized SDK vs. allow custom instrumentation? (ops preference: SDK to reduce friction).
- How should we budget SRE support across >4 pilots concurrently? (proposal: capped SRE hours + on-demand platform eng).
- Should fallback policies be globally standardized or per-team opt-in? (tradeoff: speed vs. quality consistency).

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Aisha: finalize the Operational Lab template and push to Confluence by 2026-02-05. (ENG-1402)
- Diego: prepare synthetic traffic harness repo and example load profiles by 2026-02-12. (GH PR link in linked artifacts)
- Lina: draft 3 scenario runbooks and circulate for review by 2026-02-10.
- Ravi: instrument minimal token-timing SDK and post usage snippet in the dev-x repo by 2026-02-18.
- Hannah: schedule pilot cohort kickoff and invite stakeholders (target week of 2026-02-22).

Notes to self / working thoughts (informal):
- Keep runbooks short and actionable; emphasize the first 10 minutes of triage steps.
- Consider a small "reliability ambassador" stipend for feature teams that complete the pilot early.
- Track an experiment backlog: small infra-level changes that reduce SLO friction (e.g., faster cache prefill job, more granular batch telemetry).

Appendix references (links embedded above):
- SLO Design Patterns (Confluence)
- Synthetic harness repo: ops-runbooks (GH PR #88)
- Jira EPICs: ENG-1324 (SLO operationalization), ENG-1402 (Lab template)

End of notebook.
